This confirms that insufficient sampling (coarse sampling) can lead to missing narrow peaks.

The claim states that the Post-classification Shading Pipeline (Post-DVRI) involves interpolating raw volume density values first, then mapping them to color and opacity via transfer functions, followed by shading. Source [S2] explicitly defines Post-DVRI as a pipeline where 'the original density volume f is interpolated and the resulting sample values f i are classified, via transfer functions, to yield material, opacity, and color. Shading follows immediately after classification.' Source [S1] and [S3] corroborate this by describing the post-classified model where 'raw volume values are interpolated by the rays, and the interpolation result is mapped to color and opacity' and noting that shading functions translate these interpolated values. All facts in the claim are present and consistent with the evidence.
